newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi SABIC nine-month profit falls 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Saudi SABIC nine-month profit falls 30 percent.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said profits for the first nine months of 1996 fell 30 percent to 3.415 billion riyals ($910 million).
This compares with the 4.896 billion riyal profit made in the same period last year, it said in a statement on Saturday.

SABIC, which produces about five percent of the world's petrochemicals and is the kingdom's second largest company after state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco, attributed the drop to lower international prices for many of its products.
In the first eight months of 1996 production rose four percent to 14.87 million tonnes. This was coupled with a rise in sales, which reached 11.46 million tonnes by end-August 1996.
Sales within the kingdom rose 24 percent to 758,000 tonnes.
SABIC, which employs 12,000 people in 16 industrial complexes across the kingdom, is 70 percent owned by the Saudi government. The rest is held by Saudi investors.
It posted a record 6.28 billion riyal profit for the whole of 1995, up from 4.20 billion in 1994.
